status: strongest working key conditional on the HENECOS signature crib and Sektu shifted-rhyme mechanism; not independently validated
idea: Do not force every graphic atom to a letter/string. Treat one or more adjacent subglyphs as a codepoint for a shifted phonetic transition: rhyme(previous syllable)+onset(next syllable), with initial onset and final rhyme as boundary units.
key_observation: The repeated E-rime transitions EN, EC, EB each receive a single subglyph (B2, X, U), while the more complex OS+onset transitions OSD, OSN, OST are represented by two-subglyph chunks. This is exactly the sort of complex-group splitting Sektu independently proposed in 2017.
why_this_supersedes_forced_atom_maps: It preserves the independently specified shifted-unit boundaries while avoiding arbitrary decisions such as O=O versus O=OS. Atomic splits inside OSD/OSN/OST remain secondary hypotheses to be learned from outward recurrences.

high_value_atomic_hypothesis.basis: Sektu independently proposed N could be a syllable-initial consonant such as b or d; in transition chunk DOT+N=OSD, N occupies exactly the D-onset position.
high_value_atomic_hypothesis.consequence_if_true: DOT contributes the preceding OS rime within this specific transition; whether DOT means OS context-independently remains unproved.

terminal_rule: At a true line/text boundary, the final code unit should encode only the last rime because no following onset exists. Test poem terminal classes under this rule; do not assume internal transition subglyph values transfer unchanged to terminal allographs.
falsifiers: A secure plaintext for the six-glyph line inconsistent with HENECOS DEBOSNOSTYS/A.
An independently deciphered occurrence of B2, X, or U incompatible with EN, EC, or EB respectively under the same transition phase.
Systematic evidence that cipher whitespace boundaries are strict linguistic syllable/word boundaries rather than allowing transition chunks to cross them.
N occurrences that cannot plausibly occupy onset positions when the shifted transducer is applied.
